report.tagline: The world's largest music streaming app, with podcasts and audiobooks, free with ads or paid without ads.
report.simpleSummary: Spotify lets you play almost any song, podcast or audiobook on your phone, laptop or speaker. You can use it free with ads and some limits, or pay monthly for Premium to skip ads, pick any song and download for offline. It is famous for making playlists that feel made for you, like Discover Weekly and Wrapped at the end of each year. Most of the money it earns goes to music labels and artists.

overview.whatItDoes: Spotify streams music, podcasts and audiobooks. It pays music labels, publishers and creators for the content and keeps the rest. It earns mostly from Premium subscriptions, and also from ads shown to free users. Its edge is personalisation: it learns your taste and builds playlists for you.
howItWorks: Free users can listen with ads; on phones they have limits like shuffle play and fewer skips.
Premium users pay monthly for ad-free, on-demand listening, offline downloads and higher quality, including lossless audio.
Spotify pays about two thirds of music revenue to labels and publishers based on each track's share of streams.
Algorithms build playlists like Discover Weekly, Daily Mix, Release Radar and the AI DJ.
Premium in many markets includes 15 hours a month of audiobooks.
Creators upload podcasts and video podcasts and can earn through the Spotify Partner Program.
overview.valueProposition: For listeners: almost all the world's music, plus podcasts and books, picked for your taste. For artists and podcasters: reach hundreds of millions of listeners. For advertisers: audio and video ads to a logged-in, young audience.

businessModel.summary: Spotify earns about 90% of its revenue from Premium subscriptions and about 10% from ads to free users. It pays most of that money to music labels, publishers and creators. Its profit comes from the gap, which has grown as prices rose and podcasts and audiobooks were added.

revenueStreams.detail: Individual, Duo, Family and Student plans. €4.49 billion in Q3 2026.
Audio, video and podcast ads to free users, sold directly and through automated buying. €482 million in Q3 2026.
Extra audiobook hours sold beyond the 15 hours included.
Labels and artists pay for promotion tools like Discovery Mode and Marquee.

businessModel.pricing: US Premium Individual about $11.99 to $12.99 a month after 2026 price rises, with Duo, Family and Student plans. India Premium starts around ₹139 a month per late 2025 reports, but Spotify cut India prices by about 30% in 2026 and dropped its Lite plan, so prices may be lower now. Check the site for current prices.
costDrivers: Royalties to labels and publishers, roughly two thirds of music revenue
Podcast and audiobook licensing and payouts
businessModel.unitEconomics: Take one US Premium user paying about $12 a month. About $8 goes to labels, publishers and other rights owners. Spotify keeps about $4, its 33% gross margin, then pays for servers, staff and marketing. A free user earns much less, about €1 a month in ads, but costs less in royalties. The goal is to turn free users into payers and to add audiobooks and podcasts, which pay rights owners less, to lift the margin.

howTheyGetUsers: Free tier with no time limit
Wrapped shared on social media every December
Bundles with telecoms and phone makers
Pre-installs on smart speakers, cars and TVs
whatBringsUsersBack: Weekly playlists like Discover Weekly and Release Radar
Saved playlists and libraries that are hard to move
growth.moat: Spotify knows the listening taste of almost 800 million people, which makes its recommendations better than rivals'. Users build years of playlists and liked songs, which are hard to move. Being on almost every device helps too. But all big rivals have the same music, so the moat is about experience, not content.

northStar.metric: Monthly hours of listening per active user
northStar.why: As a north star metric, listening time shows people get value from Spotify. More listening leads to higher Premium conversion, lower churn and more ad space.

pmLessons: A free tier can be your biggest marketing channel if it creates a habit that later pays.
Your margin depends on who owns the content. Spotify added podcasts and audiobooks partly to pay rights owners less per hour.
Delight can be marketing. Wrapped turns user data into something people want to share.
Price rises work only when users feel more value, so add features before raising prices.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you increase free-to-paid conversion in India?
interviewQuestions.hint: Look at price, payment (UPI autopay), local music and value. Suggest smaller plans or trials and how to test them.

interviewQuestions.question: Spotify wants more ad revenue from free users. What would you build?
interviewQuestions.hint: Split into users, hours, ad load, fill and price. Think video ads, podcasts and targeting. Add guardrails on churn.

interviewQuestions.question: Design a new feature for Spotify Wrapped.
interviewQuestions.hint: Define the goal: sharing, reactivation or conversion. Propose an idea, then define success metrics.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Spotify keep adding audiobooks and video, or focus on music?
interviewQuestions.hint: Weigh margin, competition with YouTube and Audible, and user complaints about clutter. Segment by user type.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you measure the success of the AI DJ?
interviewQuestions.hint: Pick usage, listening time, skips and retention. Compare users with and without it.
